title: Rorca — Phase 1b: Context Hydration (Schema + Git Memory)
description: Add automated context hydration to the Rorca engine. Two hydrators run as background jobs when a workspace is registered: (1) Schema Hydrator reads migration SQL files from the target project and extracts CREATE TABLE blocks — zero live DB connections, pure file parsing. (2) Git Hydrator runs a Map-Reduce pipeline over git history using cheap models for map (Haiku) and a smarter model for reduce (Sonnet), producing a dense memory.yaml. Both outputs are cached in SQLite with idempotency anchors so subsequent runs are instant delta-syncs. The Direction Stack synthesize endpoint injects both as additional sections below L3. Gate to Phase 2: hydration runs on ~/workspace, synthesized context contains schema tables and git memory sections, npm test passes with 0 failures.

userStories.title: Git Hydrator: Reduce step + POST /api/workspaces/:id/hydrate endpoint
userStories.description:
Build the reduce step (synthesizes chunk summaries into memory.yaml via Sonnet) and wire everything into a single POST endpoint that runs schema + git hydration and saves results to SQLite.

Append to backend/src/lib/git-hydrator.ts:
```typescript
export interface GitReduceOptions {
  summaries: GitChunkSummary[];
  workspaceLabel: string;
  reduceModel?: string; // default 'claude-sonnet-4-6'
}

const REDUCE_PROMPT = `You are synthesizing multiple git history summaries into a single, dense project memory document.
Output valid YAML. Use these top-level keys:

architectural_decisions:  # List of major tech choices and why
  - description: ...
    evidence: ...          # commit reference or pattern

bug_patterns:             # Recurring problems that were fixed
  - pattern: ...
    example: ...

conventions:              # Naming, data format, coding style rules discovered
  - rule: ...

awoid:                    # Approaches that were tried and abandoned
  - approach: ...
    reason: ...

Do NOT include: trivial refactors, dependency updates, formatting. 
Be dense — this YAML will be injected into every future spec generation for this project.`;

export async function gitReduceStep(options: GitReduceOptions): Promise<string> {
  const { summaries, workspaceLabel, reduceModel = 'claude-sonnet-4-6' } = options;
  
  if (summaries.length === 0) return '';
  
  // Filter out "no significant changes" summaries
  const meaningful = summaries.filter(
    s => !s.summary.toLowerCase().includes('no significant')
  );
  if (meaningful.length === 0) return '# No significant architectural patterns detected.';
  
  const combinedSummaries = meaningful
    .map((s, i) => `## Chunk ${i + 1} (${s.commitCount} commits)\n${s.summary}`)
    .join('\n\n');
  
  const prompt = `${REDUCE_PROMPT}\n\nProject: ${workspaceLabel}\n\nGit history summaries:\n${combinedSummaries}`;
  
  const result = await chatComplete([{ role: 'user', content: prompt }], reduceModel);
  return result;
}
```

Add to backend/src/routes/workspaces.ts:
POST /api/workspaces/:id/hydrate
  Body: { types?: ('schema' | 'git')[] }  // default: both
  Query: (none — workspaceId from URL param)

  Flow:
  1. Fetch workspace from DB → 404 if not found
  2. Fetch existing workspace_context row (may not exist yet)
  3. If 'schema' in types (or types empty):
     a. Call hydrateSchema(workspace.path)
     b. UPSERT into workspace_context: schema_snapshot, schema_table_count, schema_snapshot_at
     c. Insert WAL event: event_type='hydrate_schema', workspace_id, payload=JSON.stringify({tableCount})
  4. If 'git' in types (or types empty):
     a. Read last_ingested_commit_hash from workspace_context (may be null)
     b. Call gitMapStep({ workspacePath: workspace.path, fromHash: lastHash })
     c. Call gitReduceStep({ summaries, workspaceLabel: workspace.label })
     d. If fromHash was set (delta): append new memory to existing git_memory (merge YAML sections)
        If fresh run: replace git_memory entirely
     e. UPSERT into workspace_context: git_memory, last_ingested_commit_hash, git_memory_updated_at, git_commit_count
     f. Insert WAL event: event_type='hydrate_git', workspace_id, payload=JSON.stringify({commitCount, newCommits})
  5. Fetch final workspace_context row
  6. Return 200: { ok: true, schema: { tableCount, snapshot_at }, git: { commitCount, memory_updated_at, newCommits } }

  Error handling:
  - hydrateSchema returns empty → still returns 200, logs warning, schemaTableCount=0
  - gitMapStep throws (not a git repo) → return 422 { error: 'Not a git repository: ...' }
  - chatComplete throws → return 502 { error: 'LLM call failed during git reduce: ...' }

userStories.title: Phase 1b gate: manual hydration smoke test on CashflowAI
userStories.description:
Run the full test suite, then do a live hydration smoke test against the actual CashflowAI workspace to verify the entire pipeline produces real, useful context.

PHASE 1b GATE — run all steps and verify:

1. Full test suite:
   cd ~/rorca/backend && npm test
   Expected: ALL tests pass — including H-001 through H-004 tests plus all Phase 1 tests (db, workspaces, direction, yaml-parser, direction-stack, diagram-generator, specs, spec-writer, wal)
   Zero failures, zero skipped.

2. TypeScript:
   cd ~/rorca/backend && npx tsc --noEmit   (0 errors)
   cd ~/rorca && npx tsc --noEmit           (0 errors)

3. Live smoke test (start backend first: cd ~/rorca/backend && npx tsx src/server.ts):

   a. Register CashflowAI workspace (may already exist from Phase 1 E-009 smoke test):
      curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{"id":"cashflow","label":"CashflowAI","path":"/Users/dimitriteravanessian/workspace","domains":["code"]}'
      → 201 (or 409 if already exists — that's fine)

   b. Run schema hydration only (fast, no LLM):
      curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces/cashflow/hydrate \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{"types":["schema"]}'
      → {ok:true, schema:{tableCount: N}} where N > 0 (CashflowAI has 15+ tables)

   c. Verify schema was saved:
      curl -s http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces/cashflow/context | python3 -m json.tool
      → schemaSnapshot is non-null, contains 'CREATE TABLE'
      → schemaTableCount > 0

   d. Preview Direction Stack with schema:
      curl -s 'http://localhost:3030/api/direction/preview?workspaceId=cashflow&domain=code&brief=Add+a+new+API+endpoint'
      → synthesized string contains '=== DATABASE SCHEMA (Auto-Hydrated) ==='
      → synthesized string contains table names like 'workspaces' or 'imported_statement_transactions'

   e. Run git hydration (requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env, uses real LLM):
      curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces/cashflow/hydrate \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{"types":["git"]}'
      → {ok:true, git:{commitCount: N, newCommits: N}} where N > 0
      This step takes 2-5 minutes depending on commit count.

   f. Verify delta sync is fast:
      curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3030/api/workspaces/cashflow/hydrate \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{"types":["git"]}'
      → {ok:true, git:{newCommits:0}} — returns instantly (no new commits since last run)

   g. Preview Direction Stack with full context:
      curl -s 'http://localhost:3030/api/direction/preview?workspaceId=cashflow&domain=code&brief=Add+a+new+API+endpoint'
      → synthesized string contains '=== PROJECT MEMORY (Git History) ==='
      → git memory section has YAML content (architectural_decisions or conventions)

4. Commit ~/rorca/:
   cd ~/rorca && git add . && git commit -m 'feat: Phase 1b Context Hydration — Schema + Git Memory pipeline'
